summary: Quick Recipes (<=10 min) feature fully verified end-to-end. Backend (5/5 pytest passing): POST /api/quick-recipes/generate returns 200 with correct QuickRecipeResponse shape - recipes[] with name/timing/total_minutes/cuisine/difficulty/ingredients/instructions/pro_tip + speed_tips[] + count. Every returned recipe has total_minutes<=10 and non-empty ingredients+instructions (validated on 3 vegetarian/indian recipes and default-only payload). Unauthenticated -> 403. count>8 -> 400. count<1 -> 400. Frontend: registered fresh user qk_ui+<ts>@example.com. Discover mood step shows the '10-minute meals' banner (testID=open-quick) which navigates to /quick. Quick screen exposes 7 diet chips (quick-diet-{balanced,vegetarian,vegan,non-vegetarian,pescatarian,keto,gluten-free}) and 8 cuisine chips (quick-cuisine-{international,indian,italian,thai,mexican,mediterranean,chinese,american}). Selecting vegetarian + indian + tapping generate-quick fires exactly 1 POST /api/quick-recipes/generate and renders 3 RecipeCards (testID=recipe-card-<title>) each showing '<X> min' (verified: 7 min, 7 min, 8 min - all <=10), cuisine tag (Indian), difficulty, plus a 'Speed cooking hacks' tips section. Tapping a card navigates to /recipe with title, cuisine, cooking_time, difficulty, ingredients, and content params. Detail renders INSTANTLY with Ingredients + numbered Instructions from the content param and fires ZERO /api/recipes/detailed calls (verified over 6+ seconds). Save recipe + Cook hands-free buttons both present on the detail screen. Regression: snap-dish opens /import?tab=photo, scan-fridge opens /fridge, mood flow (mood happy -> meal 5 choices -> dietary 6 choices -> cuisine 11 chips) still fully functional. No React Native red screens; only benign deprecated shadow*/pointerEvents warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: quick_recipes.py total_minutes clamp: for recipes returning total_minutes<=0 or >10 the code clamps to min(max(total,1),10). This means an AI-returned recipe with e.g. total=15 would silently be re-labeled to 10 rather than dropped. Acceptable given the strict prompt, but note it may create slightly misleading timing metadata if the model ever violates the constraint.

quick.tsx openRecipe correctly passes the pre-composed markdown `content` string so /recipe renders instantly and skips /api/recipes/detailed - consistent with the Text-import 'View full recipe' and Fridge suggestions pattern.
Quick screen uses the shared RecipeCard component (which does NOT call /api/recipe-image/ai-generate for list cards) - list stays fast, matching the design goal of not generating images inline.
seed_data_creation: Registered ephemeral test users qk_ui+<ts>@example.com / Test1234 for UI flow verification (Quick Recipes works for any logged-in user; no premium needed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend contract for POST /api/quick-recipes/generate: auth required (Bearer JWT), body {count?:1-8, dietary?, cuisine?, mood?, ingredients?[], equipment?}, returns 200 {recipes:[{name,timing,total_minutes<=10,cuisine,difficulty,ingredients[],instructions[],pro_tip}], speed_tips[], count, timestamp}. Frontend Quick screen at /quick uses testIDs quick-diet-<id>, quick-cuisine-<name>, generate-quick, quick-close, recipe-card-<title>. Entry point is testID=open-quick banner on Discover MOOD step only (hidden on later steps). Tapping a card passes a `content` markdown param to /recipe so the detail renders instantly without hitting /api/recipes/detailed (same pattern as Text-import/Fridge). Cook hands-free itself is still premium-gated (button visible but tap goes to paywall) - Quick Recipes generation itself is free/trial.
rca_of_issue: N/A - new feature verification, no bugs found.
